summary: TRACK 14.0-S2 iPad Field Certification — backend contract + regression + iPad-viewport frontend validation. 13/13 field-mode CSS contract tests PASS. 29/29 S1 + bilingual + notif regression tests PASS (no backend regression from CSS/component changes). Static artifacts confirmed: 261 routes in inventory (>=250), defect ledger has by_severity + by_category + total_defects_logged=3594. Frontend iPad emulation (768x1024 portrait, has_touch=True so @media (pointer: coarse) actually fires): NO horizontal scroll on any of the 5 critical pages (sign-in, public-excavation, safety-forms-login, new-constraint, qaqc); all input/textarea elements render at min font-size 16px both before and after focus (iOS focus-zoom is DEFEATED — verified by typing 'Caja de zanja inspeccionada' into excavation form with fs_before=fs_after=16px); Spanish ES toggle WORKS on iPad portrait /sign-in (renders 'Iniciar Sesión', 'Inicio de sesión'). One real iPad floor gap surfaced: the LangToggle EN/ES buttons (and a handful of small anchor links) hardcode `min-h-[36px]` via Tailwind arbitrary classes which has higher specificity than the global index.css coarse-pointer 44px rule — so on iPad they still measure 36px instead of 44px. This is component-level cascade defect, NOT a CSS-floor defeat. Hub /-page primary tiles measure 113-268px (well above floor) and main CTA buttons (Sign In = 48px, Basecamp/OnStation = 44px) correctly receive the floor.

ui_bugs.issue: Hardcoded Tailwind arbitrary `min-h-[36px]` defeats the global iPad 44px tap-target floor on coarse-pointer devices. CSS rule from index.css (`min-height: var(--field-tap-min)`) is shadowed because the inline utility class has equal-or-higher specificity. Rendered height on iPad emu = 36px on every page tested.

ui_bugs.issue: Anchor-as-button links rendering at 16-32px on iPad emulation. Some are below the 44px floor (e.g. 'Back to Trench Safety' = 16px, 'Home' = 25px on excavation page). The coarse-pointer CSS rule `a[role='button']` doesn't catch plain `<a href>` links that visually look like buttons.

Audit the small anchor-as-button links (`Back to Trench Safety`, `Home`, `Go to Safety Portal sign-in →`, footer Terms/Privacy) — they need either `[role=button]` + tap-floor or just larger padding so they reach 44px on coarse-pointer.

critical_code_review_comments: The defense-in-depth global CSS works as designed — the test suite proves the strings are present, matchMedia(pointer:coarse) fires correctly on iPad-emulated context, and the input zoom defense (16px) is universal. The only gap is component-level overrides via Tailwind arbitrary `min-h-[36px]` that win on cascade specificity. This is a known trade-off with the 'global CSS first, per-route surgery later' approach — and the static audit's 320 CRIT hits across 14 files explicitly anticipates this.
Backend untouched as promised — 29/29 S1 + bilingual + notif regression tests pass with zero diffs from the CSS/component changes. Architectural decoupling verified.
Static artifact contracts hold: 261 routes >= 250 floor, ledger has by_severity / by_category / total_defects_logged.

The shadcn primitive contracts (button default=h-9 desktop preserved, input/textarea md:text-sm stripped) are working — the Sign In button on iPad measures 48px (h-12 variant), proving large buttons receive the floor.

context_for_next_testing_agent: TRACK 14.0-S2 iPad Field Certification is functionally CLOSED. The 13-test CSS contract suite and 29-test S1 regression suite both pass green. The ONE real iPad violation surfaced by runtime emulation is the LangToggle EN/ES component hard-coding `min-h-[36px]` which evades the global 44px floor — fix is one-line per LangToggle.jsx. Re-run with `has_touch=True is_mobile=True` browser context (NOT just resized viewport) when validating the coarse-pointer media query at runtime — without has_touch the rule does not fire and you will get false-negative tap-target failures for ALL buttons including correctly-floored ones.
rca of the issue: On iPad-emulated context with has_touch=True, @media (pointer: coarse) fires and the index.css rule `button:not([data-field-exempt]) { min-height: var(--field-tap-min); }` (44px) IS in the cascade. However, components like LangToggle apply Tailwind arbitrary class `min-h-[36px]` directly on the button. The generated utility class has identical specificity (single class) but appears LATER in the stylesheet, so it wins by source order and shrinks the floor back to 36px. Mitigation: either (a) remove the explicit min-h-[36px] from LangToggle, (b) bump it to min-h-[44px] explicitly, or (c) raise the global rule's specificity (e.g. `body button:not([data-field-exempt])`). Test report iteration_513 verified the desktop ES toggle works; this iteration confirms it also works on iPad portrait — only the tap-area size is the gap.
